This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Ryland Barton.
President Trump acknowledges that the Iran war contributed to Republicans' poor performance
during the midterm elections, but says he's not considering replacing Defense Secretary
Pete Hegseth.
NPR's Emily Fang has more on how Trump might handle the war during a new era in Washington.
He seemed to soften his stance a little today.
He said today he could end the war, quote, "any time he wanted."
He said last night on Fox & Friends that he would still strike Iran, though, if Iran,
quote, "does not behave," but also that the two countries could have a diplomatic
ending to this, that they could sign something to end the war.
He has warned that any new major strikes would happen after the midterms, but he's already
said he will not use nuclear weapons.
He told Politico last night he does not need to use nuclear weapons against Iran.
NPR's Emily Fang reporting.
Republican House Speaker Mike Johnson says he will step aside from congressional leadership
after his party's wipeout in the midterm elections.
Johnson is expected to stay on as a rank-and-file member from Louisiana when the next Congress
convenes in January.
Johnson's decision sets up a fierce internal party battle for his replacement as Republican
leader.
An organization of Hispanic and Latino Democrats in Congress will have record membership.
Rachel Cohen with member station KUNC has more.
The Congressional Hispanic Caucus projects it'll have 55 members heading into next year,
the most since the organization formed 50 years ago.
The caucus made gains in California, Texas and Colorado, where Democrat Manny Ruttenell
flipped the state's competitive 8th District.
He defeated Gabe Evans, who was also Hispanic.
Ruttenell says the large Latino community in the Denver suburbs and surrounding rural
areas were crucial to his victory.
I have the ability to speak directly to them in their native tongue in Spanish, and we
did that on news stations, we did that at churches, we did that at quinceañeras.
Associated Press polling shows Republicans appear to lose ground with Hispanic voters
this election.
For NPR News, I'm Rachel Cohen.
Mississippi's Senate race was unexpectedly competitive this midterm, and results still
aren't in.
Democratic challenger Scott Colom is about 1,000 votes ahead of incumbent Republican
Cindy Hyde-Smith, Elise Catrine-Greg of the Gulf States newsroom and Mississippi Public
Broadcasting is keeping an eye on the race.
Mississippi doesn't have runoffs or recounts for U.S. Senate races, so small swings in
the ballot count could make or break either candidate.
Both candidates say they're confident they'll win.
Here's Colom addressing supporters.
Confident wants the process laid out, where we are, where the ballots are, we're gonna
win.
And it's because the people of Mississippi turned out in historic numbers to make this
race possible in a midterm election.
Local officials in the Jackson area say it could take several days to count remaining
ballots.
For NPR News, I'm Elise Catrine-Greg in Jackson.
U.S. stocks soared today.
The Dow surged more than 1,500 points, or 3 percent.
This is NPR.
Republican attacks on critical infrastructure have caused power and water outages in Kiev
and surrounding areas that lasted hours.
Rescuers are still searching for survivors in southern Ukraine after a deadly attack
there.
Officials from the U.S., NATO, EU, and Britain are meeting in Brussels to discuss post-war
support for Ukraine.
Israel is taking the next step forward toward forming a government.
Israel's president has begun to meet with political parties to appoint one leader to
try to form a governing coalition, NPR's Daniel Estrin reports from Tel Aviv.
Israel's president began by meeting a far-right Jewish party.
The party's leaders said Arab-led parties did not have the legitimacy to be in a governing
coalition.
The president warned the party against racism.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says last week's election in Israel was, quote, "stolen,"
alleging Arab voter fraud.
Israel's top elections officials said casting doubt on the vote poses a danger to democracy.
The majority of those voted into Israel's parliament, the Knesset, are right-wing.
Israeli analyst Dalia Shenlin.
The Knesset will be dominated by ideologically right-wing parties.
And that will also set the terms of the agenda, possibly gather that kind of majority support
for various military policies coming up.
Israel and the U.S. have considered new strikes on Iran.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Among yesterday's ballot measures, Idaho voters have chosen the Winchester Model 1873
as their official state gun, also known as the gun that won the West.
It won with 31 percent of the vote, followed by 25 percent, who backed the Winchester Model
1894, and 15 percent, who backed the Colt 45.
